items.title: [Bugfix][Elastic EP] Abort prepared Elastic EP scaling on prepare failure
items.author: asdf25jae
items.summary: Fixes a crash in Elastic EP scale-up where failed preparation leaves EngineCore processes stuck waiting, causing them to crash after store timeouts.
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #69209.

When a Ray DP Elastic EP scale-up fails during preparation (for example, `DPLBAsyncMPClient._coord_store.wait` times out after 300s because new ranks cannot be scheduled), the client returns an error to the caller while existing `EngineCore` processes remain stuck inside `ElasticEPScalingState._prepare_future` (`stateless_init_dp_group` / `TCPStore` wait). When that 1800s store wait expires ~25 minutes later, `state.progress()` calls `self._prepare_future.result()` and crashes `EngineCore`.

## Changes

- **`vllm/distributed/elastic_ep/elastic_state.py`**:

items.author: alphabetc1
items.summary: Multi-turn clients resend every earlier image on each turn. For Kimi-K3, a preprocess-cache entry for a deferred-GPU image holds the decoded uint8 pixels, so the cache budget fits only a handful of images per tokenizer worker.
items.body:
## Motivation

Multi-turn clients resend every earlier image on each turn. items.title: [cfg] Batch divisibility errors do not explain the effective batch sizes
items.author: archted
items.summary: For example,,, and FSDP with 2 nodes × 3 devices produce: ## Expected Include the configured batch, rollout count, node/device counts, and backend-specific minimum-batch calculation, with guidance on which settings to adjust. Keep the validation rule unchanged…
items.body:
## Problem

Static batch validation reports only the effective batch size and minimum batch size, without showing how they were derived.

For example, `train_batch_size=4`, `rollout.n=2`, and FSDP with 2 nodes × 3 devices produce:

```text
AssertionError: real_train_batch_size (8) must be divisible by minimal possible batch size (6)
```

## Expected

Include the configured batch, rollout count, node/device counts, and backend-specific minimum-batch calculation, with guidance on which settings to adjust. Keep the validation rule unchanged.

items.title: [Perf] openai: Skip the prompt decode for text-only chats on multimodal models
items.author: maximenewman
items.summary: On a multimodal model, every chat request turns the prompt into token ids and then decodes those ids back to text. The text is only needed when the request has an image, video or audio.
items.body:
## Motivation

On a multimodal model, every chat request turns the prompt into token ids and then decodes those ids back to text. The text is only needed when the request has an image, video or audio. A text-only request sends the ids to the engine, so the text is never read.

The decode gets slower as the prompt grows and it runs on every turn of a long conversation.

## Modifications

- Skip the decode when the request has no media and its ids go to the engine.
- The render cache keeps the ids and adds the text the first time a request needs it.

items.author: amd-dlimpus
items.summary: Fixes a hang and KV cache leak in MoRIIO WRITE mode for parallel sampling (n>1) by assigning each sibling request a unique transfer_id.
items.body:
## Overview

With MoRIIO in WRITE mode, any request with `n > 1` (parallel sampling, e.g. RL rollouts) hangs forever and leaks KV on both prefill and decode. All `n` children carry the router's single `transfer_id`, and WRITE mode keys its pairing by `transfer_id` alone. This gives each child its own transfer id, `f"{transfer_id}#{i}"`, derived identically on both sides in `on_new_request`.

Same root cause as the READ-mode half of #43541 (closed as stale, unmerged), which notes the shared id clobbers `transfer_id_to_request_id`. In WRITE mode that is not the only collision, see Details.

A HiCache load-back enqueues every layer's host-to-device copy before the forward starts. items.title: [V1 FSDP] update_weights broadcasts full params every step (~9s/step on 32B); no delta or bucketed sync mode
items.author: dahai80
items.summary: On the V1 FSDP path, (actor → rollout engine weight sync) broadcasts the full parameter set every training step. Measured cost on Qwen2.5-32B TP8: ~9 s/step, every step, regardless of how few parameters changed.
items.body:
## Summary

On the V1 FSDP path, `update_weights` (actor → rollout engine weight sync) broadcasts the **full parameter set every training step**. Measured cost on Qwen2.5-32B TP8: ~9 s/step, every step, regardless of how few parameters changed. Over hundreds of GRPO steps this is a fixed tax proportional to model size, not to actual weight drift.

## Suggestion

A bucketed delta mode would remove most of this cost:

- hash/checksum per parameter bucket, sync only buckets whose checksum changed (in practice almost none change every step in RL fine-tuning — the update is small relative to init)

items.title: [Bugfix][Parser] Qwen3: repair stray <|im_start|> before function= in tool calls
items.author: georgestephanis
items.summary: Fixes Qwen3 parser silently dropping tool calls when thinking tokens (``) are emitted instead of `<` before function= declarations.
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #69190.

With thinking enabled, Qwen3.8 INT4 builds often emit the special token `<|im_start|>` where the `<` of `<function=` belongs:

```
<tool_call>
<|im_start|>function=get_weather>
<parameter=city>
Paris
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
```

The parser engine drops special tokens that have no terminal (`DROP_TERMINAL`). That leaves `function=get_weather>`, which doesn't match `FUNC_PREFIX`, so the whole call is discarded silently. The request returns `finish_reason: "stop"`, no `tool_calls` and no content.

items.author: hlin99

items.body:

The failure was introduced by [vllm-project/vllm#69013](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69013) (`1bdc437402`), which removed `validate_runtime()` and its calls from the HY4 Flash text and multimodal constructors. items.title: [Perf][XPU] Run the fp32 lm_head through torch.mm(out_dtype=float32) on XPU
items.author: mgaruccio
items.summary: has a fast path for that accumulates the bf16/fp16 projection directly into fp32 with (#48390). It is gated to CUDA and ROCm, so on XPU every decode step falls back to casting the hidden states and the whole lmhead weight to fp32 before the GEMM.
items.body:
## Overview

`LogitsProcessor._apply_head` has a fast path for `head_dtype=float32` that
accumulates the bf16/fp16 projection directly into fp32 with
`torch.mm(..., out_dtype=torch.float32)` (#48390). It is gated to CUDA and ROCm,
so on XPU every decode step falls back to casting the hidden states **and the whole
lm_head weight** to fp32 before the GEMM. `torch.mm(out_dtype=float32)` with
bf16/fp16 inputs is implemented on XPU (torch 2.15.0+xpu, the version pinned in
`requirements/xpu.txt`), so this PR takes the same path there.

## Claims

- Removes the per-step fp32 copy of the lm_head weigh

## Motivation

Gemma 4 E2B/E4B encode audio with a 12-layer conformer that runs eagerly, one clip at a time. Prefill batches rarely hold more than one new audio request, so on ASR traffic the tower sets TTFT and caps throughput.

## Motivation

Item 6 of #49055: with `--log-requests`, the Rust server's request log goes through one process-wide `tracing-appender` writer with a 1,024-line, non-lossy buffer, behind a global mutex. Once a slow log collector fills the buffer, `write_all` blocks the tokio worker while it holds that mutex, so every other worker that logs stalls behind it, and unrelated requests and health checks on every listener stop being served until the collector catches up.

items.title: [Perf][Model] Inkling 2: back only readable sconv-state blocks on SM12x
items.author: abtraore
items.summary: Reduces Inkling 2 sconv-state memory allocation on SM12x by backing only readable blocks, cutting per-group reserve from 514 to 9 blocks and enabling ~548K max model length.
items.body:
## Overview

Inkling 2 stores its 48 short-conv states (W=4) as tiny-window sliding-window KV groups, and each request reserves `W - 1 + max_in_flight_tokens` positions of bf16 conv state per group even though a later step only reads the 3 positions before its first token. On SM12x with TP=1 this PR backs only the blocks a later step or a prefix hit can read (DFlash-style null leading blocks) and skips conv-state stores into the null block. Addresses #54703 for Inkling 2 on SM12x.

## Claims

- RTX 5090 (32 GB), `thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini`, FP8 KV, one GPU: the per-request conv-state r

items.title: [Perf] qwen3-asr: Replay the audio tower from token-budget CUDA graphs
items.author: ruiling-smartbear
items.summary: The Qwen3-Omni audio tower, which Qwen3-ASR reuses, runs eagerly and blocks on the GPU several times per call: -, and in the forward. ASR clips are short, so the tower is launch-bound.
items.body:
## Motivation

The Qwen3-Omni audio tower, which Qwen3-ASR reuses, runs eagerly and blocks on the GPU several times per call:
- `chunk_lengths.tolist()`, `.max().item()` and `aftercnn_lens.tolist()` in the forward.
- A `max_seqlen` read in every encoder layer.

ASR clips are short, so the tower is launch-bound. Under load, its time shows up directly in TTFT and tail latency.

items.title: [Perf] mem_cache: Cut unified-memory relocation cost once the pool fills
items.author: dcw02
items.summary: With, the sliding-window band sits between the Mamba-state band and the full-attention band. Once the pool fills, nearly every allocation relocates it, and on each relocation is expensive: - Slack between bands is split by expected growth in pages.
items.body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-unified-memory`, the sliding-window band sits between the Mamba-state band and the full-attention band. Once the pool fills, nearly every allocation relocates it, and on `main` each relocation is expensive:

- Slack between bands is split by expected growth in pages. A Mamba state is 32 MB and a window token is 12 KB, so the gap beside the states gets too little room and the window is pushed again and again while the pool fills.
- Each relocation walks every page of the window's span on the host: about 290 ms for a 1.2 million-page window at page size 1.

## Motivation

Kimi-K3's content-addressed multimodal preprocess cache defaults to 256 MiB in total, and that budget is divided across tokenizer workers. Multi-turn clients resend every earlier image on each turn, so most of those images miss the cache and are decoded and preprocessed again on every request.

- Raise `KimiK3ImageProcessor.auto_mm_preprocess_cache_size_mb` from 256 to 16384, so each tokenizer worker can keep the images of its active sessions.

items.title: [Fix] multimodal: Bound request-supplied dynamic patch caps
items.author: saitarrun
items.summary: ,, and are accepted as plain request fields with no upper bound. The InternVL processor resolves them with only a lower bound and passes the result to, which enumerates aspect-ratio candidates in a triple loop whose iteration count grows quadratically with the…
items.body:
## Motivation

`max_dynamic_patch`, `image_max_dynamic_patch`, and `video_max_dynamic_patch` are accepted as plain `Optional[int]` request fields with no upper bound. The InternVL processor resolves them with only a lower bound (`max(1, int(...))`) and passes the result to `dynamic_preprocess`, which enumerates aspect-ratio candidates in a triple loop whose iteration count grows quadratically with the cap (650 iterations at the default of 12, ~2.7M at 200, ~3.3e17 at 999999). A single request with an absurd cap therefore burns unbounded CPU before the expanded token count is ever checked again

items.title: [Perf] diffusion/minimax_h3: decode VAE image frames into a cached pinned host buffer
items.author: Woody-Hu
items.summary: The MiniMax-H3-Image decode stage copies VAE-decoded image frames to the host with a pageable transfer. Pageable DtoH over PCIe runs at a few hundred MB/s, so each 50 MB fp32 frame costs 19-35 ms of decode time per request.
items.body:
## Motivation

The MiniMax-H3-Image decode stage copies VAE-decoded image frames to the host with a pageable `.cpu()` transfer. Pageable DtoH over PCIe runs at a few hundred MB/s, so each 50 MB fp32 frame costs 19-35 ms of decode time per request.

## Modifications

- Route the decoded frame through `_to_pinned_cpu()`, which copies it into a per-`(shape, dtype, device)` cached pinned host buffer (LRU cap 8) instead of a pageable `.cpu()`.
- The `cudaHostAlloc` / page-lock cost is paid once per shape; every subsequent DtoH runs at full PCIe link bandwidth (6.66 GB/s measured on A100 PCIe Gen3).

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] wvSplitK: packed bf16 dot on gfx950
items.author: mawong-amd
items.summary: Two changes, one idea: the rows of the tile table only pay off when takes them; when the shape routes to the fragmented tile, which loses to at for every dtype — so those shapes now fall back to on wave64. And on gfx950, bf16 uses the packed dot instead of the…
items.body:
## Overview

Two changes, one idea: the `YTILE 3/4` rows of the `wvSplitK` tile table only pay off when `sml_` takes them (`M % tile == 0`); when `M % tile != 0` the shape routes to the fragmented `hf_` tile, which loses to `sml_` at `YTILE 2` for every dtype — so those shapes now fall back to `YTILE 2` on wave64. And on gfx950, bf16 uses the packed `v_dot2_f32_bf16` dot instead of the MFMA path whose `floatx4` accumulators spill at `YTILE 3/4`, so the N=5 bf16 `YTILE=2` pin drops there. gfx942/gfx90a keep MFMA and the pin; their device code is unchanged.

`__HIP__MI3XX__` stays the family

items.author: yingluobailu
items.summary: An otherwise valid workload can yield zero requests after filtering. For example, a ShareGPT context limit can reject all conversations.
items.body:
## Motivation
An otherwise valid workload can yield zero requests after filtering. For example, a ShareGPT context limit can reject all conversations. The Python serving benchmark indexes the first row to detect multi-turn requests, or to construct the warmup request for Mooncake, and raises `IndexError` without explaining the input problem. This also happens with `--warmup-requests 0`.

## Modifications
- Validate that the workload contains requests before prompt inspection and warmup construction.
- Include the dataset name in the error and point to the dataset filters and `--num-prompts`.

## Description

Fixes #22733.

In thinking mode the Kimi-K2.5 chat template prefills `<think>`. ## Overview

Add `--monokernel-layers N`: with `--monokernel`, run the DeepSeek-V4.1 mono decode path on decoder layers with layer id below N only; the remaining layers take vLLM's standard path and keep no kernel weight copies. This is what lets the gfx942 fused decode run on a 192 GB MI300X at TP4, where the copies of all 40 layers (#60731) do not fit next to the KV cache, and it is the KV-room knob at TP8 for high concurrency. # What does this PR do?

Adds `lm_head_loss_num_chunks` (`--lm-head-loss-num-chunks`, default 1 = off). items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: Replaces per-batch penalty tables with a per-request PenaltyStatusPool that updates token counts immediately after sampling on the sampling stream, eliminating cross-stream races and enabling exact speculative penalties.

## Motivation

Sampling penalties need each request's output history. On main that history lives in per-batch penalizer tables: the scheduler fills them from the host `output_ids` in `prepare_for_decode`, which lags one step under overlap, and filters and merges them on the schedule stream while a forward may still read them. Exact speculative penalties (the next PR) need the history current at verify and owned by the device.

## Overview

On gfx942 (MI300X/MI325X), the DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 sparse MLA decode launches `_sparse_attn_decode_partial_kernel` with one workgroup per 16 heads, so a rank with 32 or more heads gathers and dequantizes every KV tile once per 16 heads. The parser converts PIL images to RGB, but a video passed as a list of PIL frames keeps each frame's own mode. Grayscale, RGBA and palette frames therefore fail in the HF processors. This PR converts PIL video frames with `convert_image_mode(frame, "RGB")`, the same call used for PIL images.

Small Models Harness passes by a single question, and the ROCm 10.1 update (#62536) pushes it below the
threshold. This PR subtracts the zero-point term from the exact int32 accumulator inside the Triton kernel, on
ROCm only.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/7126024][fix] Release checkpoint cache before post-load transforms
items.author: trtllm-agent
items.summary: Addresses https://nvbugs/7126024. Long-lived post-load tensors, including fused GDN input-projection weights, can split large cached checkpoint allocations. [Discussion: The existing cache release after model finalization remains in place.]
items.body:
## Description

Addresses https://nvbugs/7126024.

Long-lived post-load tensors, including fused GDN input-projection weights, can split large cached checkpoint allocations. The unused tails then remain reserved when KV-cache profiling runs, even after its existing cache cleanup.

items.title: [Bugfix][Attention] TRTLLM prefill with BF16 query and FP8 KV applies k/v scales once
items.author: hao-aaron
items.summary: This path first dequantizes the pages it reads with, which already multiplies K by and V by; the kernel then also got and. Prefill and decode disagreed whenever the scales were not 1.0 (cold-start bug). [Discussion: ✅ Triggered for commit.]
items.body:
## Purpose

TRTLLM prefill with a BF16 query and an FP8 KV cache applied the k/v scales twice. This path first dequantizes the pages it reads with `trtllm_prefill_attn_kvfp8_dequant`, which already multiplies K by `k_scale` and V by `v_scale`; the kernel then also got `bmm1_scale = scale · q_scale · k_scale` and `bmm2_scale = v_scale`. Prefill and decode disagreed whenever the scales were not 1.0 (cold-start bug). The kernel now gets `bmm1_scale = scale` and `bmm2_scale = 1.0` on this path; a BF16 query has no `q_scale` and no fused output quant (that requires an FP8 query). Part of RFC #54477

items.title: [XPU] Accept FLEX_ATTENTION as an explicit attention backend
items.author: songhappy
items.summary: This honors an explicit request, like the existing explicit one. Default selection is unchanged. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Purpose

`XPUPlatform.get_attn_backend_cls` raises "Invalid attention backend for xpu" when `FLEX_ATTENTION` is requested explicitly, although the FlexAttention backend runs on XPU: `torch` flex attention compiles through Triton XPU, and the backend's only CUDA-specific code is guarded by `torch.cuda.is_available()`. This honors an explicit `FLEX_ATTENTION` request, like the existing explicit `TRITON_ATTN` one. Default selection is unchanged.

It lets callers that need the generator to use the same attention kernel as their trainer (e.g. TorchTitan RL, pytorch/torchtitan#5402) run on XPU.

items.title: [ROCm][Perf][MoE] Keep a 32-column BF16 intermediate pad for AITER on CDNA3
items.author: frida-andersson
items.summary: On CDNA3, vLLM now passes AITER the 32-column intermediate pad of an unquantized MoE instead of rounding it down to 0, so AITER's gfx942 BF16 FlyDSL decode kernels skip the zero tail (ROCm/aiter#8411). Qwen3.8-Flash-Next BF16 at TP4 has 160 intermediate column…
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Summary

On CDNA3, vLLM now passes AITER the 32-column intermediate pad of an unquantized MoE instead of rounding it down to 0, so AITER's gfx942 BF16 FlyDSL decode kernels skip the zero tail (ROCm/aiter#8411). Qwen3.8-Flash-Next BF16 at TP4 has 160 intermediate columns per rank, stored as 192, and today every expert computes and reads the 32 zero columns at the end of each Gate/Up half and of Down's K. Skipping them makes the MoE 8–13% faster from 1 to 256 tokens.

On 4× MI325X, TP4, MTP-3:

* up to 5.3% more output throughput (1K input, concurrency 8)

items.author: LeizhenZhang

items.body:
## Overview

The `pythonic`, `llama4_pythonic`, `olmo3` and `lfm2` tool parsers rescan the whole tool call text in Python on every streamed delta. The asyncio event loop of that API server process is blocked for that time. This PR makes the shared helpers in `vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py` jump over string bodies with a regex search. items.title: [Perf][Core] Pack the consumed audio of streaming sessions
items.author: andylolu2
items.summary: Stacked on #68539: only the last commit, 6201477, is new here. A streaming input session keeps the feature of every audio chunk, so that it can replay them after a preemption.
items.body:
## Overview

Stacked on #68539: only the last commit, 6201477, is new here.

A streaming input session keeps the feature of every audio chunk, so that it can replay them after a preemption. Each kept feature is about 15 objects that the cyclic GC tracks, across the scheduler and the workers. A full collection therefore gets slower the longer a session runs. This PR packs the features of the chunks that have been consumed into arrays and a few byte buffers, so each one leaves no tracked objects behind.

This is a proof of concept, opened as a draft. It has no end-to-end serving benchmark yet.

items.title: [Perf] Load saved FlashInfer tactics before DS4.1F TP4 decode warmup
items.author: matteso1
items.summary: FlashInfer benchmarks several kernel tactics for an operation and input shape, then saves the winner in a per-rank table. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash’s TP4 low-latency decode starts that search inside.
items.body:
## Overview

FlashInfer benchmarks several kernel tactics for an operation and input shape, then saves the winner in a per-rank table. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash’s TP4 low-latency decode starts that search inside `load_model`. On a warm restart all four tables can already be on disk. The normal warmup reads them after `load_model`, so the decode has already paid to find the same winners again.

Moving the read earlier on its own can still miss. In one reproduction, the early key used a KV block size of 64 and the saved table used the backend’s resolved size of 128. This patch resolves the block size

items.title: [trainer, worker, algo] fix: whiten advantages per mini-batch chunk in TrainingWorker
items.author: Doublrest
items.summary: In V1 trainers ( and ), whitens advantages once over the full sampled batch, whereas splits the batch into optimizer chunks without re-normalizing per chunk. When the sampled batch is larger than, individual optimizer chunks can have non-zero token-weighted ad…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8766.

In V1 trainers (`sync` and `colocate_async`), `_compute_advantage()` whitens advantages once over the full sampled batch, whereas `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()` splits the batch into `ppo_mini_batch_size` optimizer chunks without re-normalizing per chunk. When the sampled batch is larger than `ppo_mini_batch_size`, individual optimizer chunks can have non-zero token-weighted advantage means, introducing chunk-level policy-gradient drift.

This PR re-normalizes `mini_batch_td["advantages"]` per optimizer chunk in `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()`

items.body:
## Summary

On verl v0.9.1, verl's own Qwen2-7B-Instruct GRPO GSM8K recipe (the `qwen2-7b-fsdp2.log` baseline in `docs/algo/baseline.md`) crashed twice on 8x B200, both times on the first training step after a validation pass. Right before the crash, the agent-loop workers log `Timeout waiting for data status update ACK from controller after 30s` and carry on. The data was written to storage but the controller never marks it ready, so the trainer later gets an empty batch from TransferQueue and fails with `KeyError: 'loss_mask'` in `compute_log_prob`.

The timeout itself is a slow controller.

items.author: GaokaiZhang
items.summary: An engine that dies in that window stays registered in the router and in the engine list. The next sends it, the request fails with, and the run stops.
items.body:
## Problem

The health monitors are paused from the end of a rollout (`finish_rollout`) to the weight update. An engine that dies in that window stays registered in the router and in the engine list. The next `update_weights` sends it `pause_generation`, the request fails with `ConnectionRefusedError`, and the run stops. With the fully-async rollout the periodic check does not help either: each resume restarts the first wait (600 s by default), so no periodic check runs when a rollout takes less than that. Details and the traceback: #2551.

## Description

A context or generation worker can fail to transfer KV state for a valid request. The coordinator sends the per-request error across executor IPC as a string. The OpenAI worker then returns HTTP 400, which tells clients to change their input and can suppress a retry of the full request.

Return HTTP 503 for the two transfer errors emitted by the disaggregation coordinator. The router already forwards the worker’s HTTP status. A client can retry the full request with a new worker pair.

items.body:
## Description

This PR adds DeCo-Attention to VisualGen as an opt-in quantized-attention recipe of the `CUTEDSL` backend. The QK product of self-attention runs on NVFP4 operands, with the quantization error of the scores compensated inside the same matrix product; the PV product runs in FP8, or in NVFP4 on SM120. On Wan2.2 T2V at 720p the denoising is 1.68x faster than with BF16 attention on GB300, 1.73x on Rubin and 1.69x to 1.85x on RTX PRO 6000.

It is off by default and enabled per configuration:

```yaml
attention_config:
  backend: CUTEDSL
  quant_attention_config:
    qk_dtype: nvfp4
discussion:

items.summary: This PR lets git worktrees of TensorRT-LLM share one ccache. A fresh worktree then reuses the objects that another worktree already compiled, so its first build is much faster.
items.body:
## Description

This PR lets git worktrees of TensorRT-LLM share one ccache. A fresh worktree then reuses the objects that another worktree already compiled, so its first build is much faster.

Before this PR, a fresh worktree missed ccache for every compile. ccache keys each object on its compile command, and that command holds the absolute paths of the source and build folders. A worktree at a new path therefore gets new keys. ccache's `base_dir` setting fixes this, but each user has to configure it. CI configures it in `jenkins/controlCCache.groovy`.

This PR adds `cpp/cmake/modules/ccache.

items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

**Problem.** A `kv_cache_compression_config` method with a cold-page codec (today `quantization_for_cold_page`, NVFP4) makes `KVCacheManagerV2` encode pages when they leave the GPU for its host, disk or remote tiers. The `mooncake-store` connector takes the place of those tiers (it forces `host_cache_size` / `disk_cache_size` to 0 for roles that transfer KV), but it moved raw GPU pages, so with both configured the compression setting silently had no effect on the pool.

**Solution.** The connector now stores pages through the KV cache manager's own codec

items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

The qwen4_exp cache manager keeps a QSA index-key plane next to the K/V pool. A page holds one row per token (`tokens_per_block`, 32): the token's raw index key, overwritten at the last token of each `compress_ratio` group by the group's compressed key. Index scoring reads only the compressed keys; a raw key is read once more, to pool its group, and is dead after that.

items.title: [Feature Request]Support FP32 bias gradient accumulation in native fused Linear backward
items.author: zjjott
items.summary: Extends fused linear backward to accumulate bias gradients in FP32 instead of BF16, reducing split/full gradient error from ~1e-3 to ~1e-7.
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

When `gradient_accumulation_fusion=True`, native `LinearWithGradAccumulationAndAsyncCommunication` can accumulate weight gradients directly into FP32 `main_grad`, but its bias gradient still passes through BF16 before reaching the FP32 DDP buffer.

The relevant code is [`grad_bias = grad_output.sum(dim=0)` in layers.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/dev/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/layers.py#L962). With BF16 `grad_output`, this returns a BF16 result. Subsequent FP32 accumulation cannot recover the lost precision.

items.title: fix(moe): count unmasked tokens exactly when rank lengths differ
items.author: ilml
items.summary: gettokensperexpertandtokencount derived totalnumtokens as locallength groupsize when no padding mask is given. Ranks in one MoE statistics domain can hold different numbers of tokens (variable-length or compacted inputs, runtime CP), so the aux losses were nor…
items.body:
get_tokens_per_expert_and_token_count derived total_num_tokens as local_length * group_size when no padding mask is given. Ranks in one MoE statistics domain can hold different numbers of tokens (variable-length or compacted inputs, runtime CP), so the aux losses were normalized, and with per-token loss scaled, by the wrong count.

Carry this rank's row count in the same all-reduce as the per-expert counts, so the total is exact and no extra collective is added. The unmasked total_num_tokens is now a 0-d tensor, as the masked one already was.

items.title: [algo, trainer, fsdp, megatron, cfg, doc] feat: add topk_rb KL loss (top-k Rao-Blackwellised KL to the reference)
items.author: hiddevandebeek
items.summary: It adds, a KL penalty against the reference policy for. The estimator computes KL(πθ ‖ πref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Implements the RFC in #8536. It adds `actor.kl_loss_type: topk_rb`, a KL penalty against the reference policy for `use_kl_loss=True`.

The estimator computes KL(π_θ ‖ π_ref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket. The within-tail part is estimated from the sampled token, so the result is an **unbiased** estimate of the full-vocabulary KL gradient at every k, with much lower variance than the single-sample `kl`/`k2`/`low_var_kl`/`k3+` options. It is the per-token Rao-Blackwellised KL of [Amini et al., NeurIPS 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.1063

## Summary

When context compaction splits an episode into multiple training rows, `rollout/raw_reward` gives that episode extra weight. Compute the mean over episodes before data-parallel partitioning. Each episode contributes equally, including when its segments land on different ranks. In the example above, the logged mean stays at `0.25` after splitting.

### What does this PR do?

Preserve vLLM's `finish_reason="length"` in `TokenOutput.stop_reason`. Today the vLLM rollout server reports `completed` both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. A caller translating this value to the Anthropic Messages API consequently sends `end_turn` for a truncated response, and the client can exit with work still in progress.

### Design and compatibility

Map vLLM's `stop` to `completed` and let `length` pass through the existing fallback. Callers can now return `max_tokens` to Anthropic clients. Abort still maps to `aborted`

Rank 0 creates the --save-hf directory and copies the non-weight files of --hf-checkpoint into it, then the

already exists on the server.

goes to the server and refreshes the cached entry; where the directory is already visible it does nothing.

items.title: [reward] fix: compare prime_code call-based outputs as plain builtins
items.author: Aarav500
items.summary: In, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of or whose always returns got full reward on every call-based task.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8656. In `prime_code`, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with `output == expected`. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of `int` or `list` whose `__eq__` always returns `True` got full reward on every call-based task. Swapping the operands doesn't help, because Python tries a subclass's reflected `__eq__` first.

This adds `_to_builtin()` in `prime_code/testing_util.py` and applies it to the output right after the existing `json.dumps(output)` call. It rebuilds the value from plain `None`/`bool`/`int`/`float

items.body:
### Bug Description

items.author: ttqiao1617
items.summary: Megatron's policy snapshots currently save parameters but omit persistent model buffers. If a buffer such as changes during training, restoring the old snapshot can leave a mix of old parameters and newer routing state.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8632.

Megatron's policy snapshots currently save parameters but omit persistent model buffers. Checkpoint participants each own one GPU, but Ray's default first barrier can enroll every visible GPU and its rendezvous key contains the local ordinal. The engine now owns a device-bound NCCLGroup specialization with a single-device barrier and a logical group key shared across masked/shared ordinal layouts. items.author: R0k1e
items.summary: upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with, so the whole logits tensor is copied to fp32.
items.body:
## Motivation

`Float16Module.forward` upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with `labels=None`, so the whole `[T, V]` logits tensor is copied to fp32. The LM head GEMM has already rounded these values to bf16, so the copy adds memory but no precision. It is the largest single allocation in a long-context actor step: 40,960 tokens × 248,320 vocabulary is about 41 GB in fp32 versus 20 GB in bf16.

The fp32 copy does one useful thing: every consumer of the logits computes in fp32 because its input is fp32. This PR keeps that guarantee, but enforces it

The values at response tokens are unchanged.

With `--partial-rollout`, a sample aborted mid-generation goes back to the data buffer and is resumed later. `generate()` resumes it with a `max_new_tokens` budget reduced by `sample.response_length` and appends the new tokens after the existing response, so the request must be conditioned on that response.

items.author: 0z5a

items.body:
## Problem

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

How it happens:

- slime's colocated sender calls `update_weights_from_tensor` with `serialized_named_tensors`, `load_format="flattened_bucket"` and `weight_version`. It sets neither `selector` nor `disable_draft_model`.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

## Background

## Background

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds the Vime-side provider boundary required to run RL-Kernel train/rollout consistency on CUDA while keeping Vime responsible for token layout, masking, loss composition, and framework orchestration.

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

`--kl-coef` is reward-KL shaping. GRPO-style estimators (`grpo`, `gspo`, `cispo`) do not apply KL to rewards, so a non-zero `--kl-coef` is a silent no-op today.

Fixes #1369.

`distributed_masked_whiten(..., shift_mean=False)` used to center, scale, then add the mean back:

items.author: yuyz-cyber

## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.title: require --ref-load when KL is enabled instead of crashing with a TypeError
items.author: rootkiller6788
items.summary: Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slimevalidateargs with, because it stat'd args.refload before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.
items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

items.title: fix: preserve equals in extra environment values
items.author: imshunsuke
items.summary: For example: was parsed as: This corrupts padded or otherwise -containing environment values. JSON input handling and the existing fallback tokenization remain unchanged.
items.body:
## Summary

- Preserve `=` characters after the first separator in the space-separated `extra_env_vars` fallback parser.
- Add regression coverage to the always-on CPU test matrix.

## Problem

`_parse_extra_env_vars` split each assignment on every `=` and then kept only the second component. For example:

`TOKEN=abc== END=ok`

was parsed as:

`{"TOKEN": "abc", "END": "ok"}`

This corrupts padded or otherwise `=`-containing environment values.

## Change

Use `split("=", 1)` so only the key/value separator is consumed. JSON input handling and the existing fallback tokenization remain unchanged

I was poking at `--multimodal-keys` with a dataset that mixes image rows and plain
text rows, and ended up finding three separate problems in `_build_messages`.

### The prompt gets shattered when a row has no media

The placeholder split builds a regex alternation out of whatever media the row
actually carries. When the media column is `None` nothing goes into that set, the
pattern collapses to `"()"`, and that matches the empty string at every position:

```python
>>> from vime.utils.data import _build_messages
>>> _build_messages({"text": "Describe this image.", "images": None},
...
discussion:
